title: Telling Stories
subtitle: Narrate the past like a French storyteller

lessons.title: Il était une fois
lessons.description: Master the dance between passé composé and imparfait to tell vivid stories.

blocks.heading: Two past tenses, two jobs
blocks.body: French stories weave two past tenses together. The imparfait paints the background: descriptions, habits, ongoing situations, feelings. The passé composé reports the events — completed actions that push the story forward. Think of the imparfait as the scenery and the passé composé as the actors walking across the stage.

examples.french: Il faisait nuit et la rue était déserte.
examples.english: It was dark and the street was deserted.

examples.french: Soudain, quelqu'un a frappé à la porte.
examples.english: Suddenly, someone knocked on the door.

examples.french: Quand j'étais petit, je passais l'été chez ma grand-mère.
examples.english: When I was little, I used to spend the summer at my grandmother's.

examples.french: Un jour, j'ai trouvé une vieille lettre dans le grenier.
examples.english: One day, I found an old letter in the attic.

examples.french: Elle lisait tranquillement quand le téléphone a sonné.
examples.english: She was reading quietly when the phone rang.

blocks.tip: Ask yourself: is this the backdrop (imparfait) or does it move the plot forward (passé composé)?

blocks.heading: Setting the scene with the imparfait
blocks.body: Use the imparfait for weather, time, age, physical descriptions and emotions in the past. These details answer "what was it like?" rather than "what happened?". A good story usually opens with several imparfait sentences before the first event arrives.

examples.french: Il pleuvait depuis le matin.
examples.english: It had been raining since morning.

examples.french: J'avais dix ans et je rêvais d'aventures.
examples.english: I was ten years old and I dreamed of adventures.

examples.french: Le village semblait endormi.
examples.english: The village seemed asleep.

examples.french: Nous avions peur, mais nous étions curieux.
examples.english: We were afraid, but we were curious.

examples.french: Ma grand-mère racontait toujours des histoires étranges.
examples.english: My grandmother always told strange stories.

blocks.heading: Signal words
blocks.body: Certain expressions almost always call for one tense or the other. "Autrefois", "à l'époque", "tous les jours", "d'habitude" signal the imparfait. "Un jour", "soudain", "tout à coup", "une fois" announce a passé composé event.

examples.french: Autrefois, on vivait sans téléphone portable.
examples.english: In the old days, people lived without mobile phones.

examples.french: À l'époque, je ne parlais pas français.
examples.english: At the time, I didn't speak French.

examples.french: Un jour, tout a changé.
examples.english: One day, everything changed.

examples.french: D'habitude, il rentrait tôt, mais ce soir-là, il est rentré à minuit.
examples.english: Usually he came home early, but that evening he came home at midnight.

blocks.tip: "Il était une fois..." (once upon a time) opens every French fairy tale — in the imparfait, of course!

blocks.heading: Choosing the tense: a checklist
blocks.body: Description, habit, ongoing state → imparfait (je parlais, il faisait, nous avions). Completed event, sudden change, sequence of actions → passé composé (j'ai parlé, il a fait, nous avons eu). When one action interrupts another, the ongoing action is imparfait and the interruption is passé composé.

examples.french: Je dormais quand tu as appelé.
examples.english: I was sleeping when you called.

examples.french: Pendant que nous marchions, il a commencé à pleuvoir.
examples.english: While we were walking, it started to rain.

examples.french: Elle a ouvert la fenêtre parce qu'il faisait chaud.
examples.english: She opened the window because it was hot.

examples.french: Ils ont vécu dix ans à Paris.
examples.english: They lived in Paris for ten years.

blocks.tip: A finished period with clear limits (dix ans, toute la journée) takes the passé composé, even if it lasted long.

blocks.heading: Meaning changes
blocks.body: Some verbs change meaning depending on the tense. "Je savais" = I knew (state); "j'ai su" = I found out (event). "Je voulais" = I wanted; "j'ai voulu" = I tried / decided to. "Je connaissais" = I knew (a person/place); "j'ai connu" = I met.

examples.french: Je savais qu'il habitait ici.
examples.english: I knew he lived here.

examples.french: J'ai su la vérité hier soir.
examples.english: I found out the truth last night.

examples.french: Elle connaissait bien ce quartier.
examples.english: She knew this neighborhood well.

examples.french: J'ai connu ma femme à Lyon.
examples.english: I met my wife in Lyon.

passages.title: La maison au bout du chemin
passages.french:
Quand j'étais enfant, nous passions chaque été chez ma grand-mère, en Dordogne.
Sa maison se trouvait au bout d'un petit chemin, entourée de noyers.
Tous les matins, je me levais tôt et j'allais chercher le pain avec mon cousin.
La boulangère nous connaissait bien et nous donnait toujours un bonbon.
Un été, pourtant, quelque chose d'étrange est arrivé.
Un soir d'orage, nous avons entendu un bruit bizarre dans le grenier.
Ma grand-mère lisait près de la cheminée ; elle a levé les yeux, très calme.
« Ce sont les chauves-souris », a-t-elle dit en souriant.
Mais mon cousin et moi, nous ne l'avons pas crue.
Nous avons pris une lampe et nous sommes montés doucement.
Le grenier était sombre et sentait la poussière.
Dans un coin, nous avons découvert une vieille malle pleine de lettres.
C'étaient les lettres que mon grand-père écrivait pendant la guerre.
Cette nuit-là, j'ai compris que chaque famille cache des histoires extraordinaires.
passages.english:
When I was a child, we spent every summer at my grandmother's, in Dordogne.
Her house stood at the end of a little path, surrounded by walnut trees.
Every morning, I got up early and went to get the bread with my cousin.
The baker knew us well and always gave us a sweet.
One summer, however, something strange happened.
One stormy evening, we heard a weird noise in the attic.
My grandmother was reading by the fireplace; she looked up, very calm.
"It's the bats," she said with a smile.
But my cousin and I didn't believe her.
We took a lamp and went up quietly.
The attic was dark and smelled of dust.
In a corner, we discovered an old trunk full of letters.
They were the letters my grandfather wrote during the war.
That night, I understood that every family hides extraordinary stories.

lessons.title: Avant cela...
lessons.description: Use the plus-que-parfait to talk about what had happened before another past event.

blocks.heading: A past before the past
blocks.body: The plus-que-parfait describes an action completed BEFORE another past action. English uses "had done"; French uses the imparfait of avoir or être + past participle. It lets your listener travel one step further back in time.

examples.french: Quand je suis arrivé, le train était déjà parti.
examples.english: When I arrived, the train had already left.

examples.french: Elle a raté l'examen parce qu'elle n'avait pas révisé.
examples.english: She failed the exam because she hadn't studied.

examples.french: Nous avons visité le musée dont tu nous avais parlé.
examples.english: We visited the museum you had told us about.

examples.french: Il pleuvait, et j'avais oublié mon parapluie.
examples.english: It was raining, and I had forgotten my umbrella.

examples.french: Ils étaient fatigués parce qu'ils s'étaient couchés tard.
examples.english: They were tired because they had gone to bed late.

blocks.tip: If you can say "had + past participle" in English, the plus-que-parfait is almost always right in French.

blocks.heading: Formation
blocks.body: Take the imparfait of avoir (j'avais, tu avais, il avait...) or être (j'étais, tu étais...) and add the past participle. The same verbs that use être in the passé composé (aller, venir, partir, and all reflexives) use être here too, and the participle agrees.

examples.french: j'avais fini
examples.english: I had finished

examples.french: tu avais dit
examples.english: you had said

examples.french: elle était partie
examples.english: she had left

examples.french: nous nous étions perdus
examples.english: we had gotten lost

examples.french: ils avaient promis
examples.english: they had promised

blocks.heading: Time markers of anteriority
blocks.body: Words like "déjà" (already), "la veille" (the day before), "auparavant" (beforehand) and "avant" often accompany the plus-que-parfait. "Le lendemain" (the next day) then brings the story back forward.

examples.french: La veille, il avait plu toute la journée.
examples.english: The day before, it had rained all day.

examples.french: J'avais déjà vu ce film.
examples.english: I had already seen this film.

examples.french: Elle avait vécu à Rome auparavant.
examples.english: She had lived in Rome beforehand.

examples.french: Le lendemain, tout le monde avait oublié l'incident.
examples.english: The next day, everyone had forgotten the incident.

blocks.tip: "La veille" and "le lendemain" are the storyteller's versions of "hier" and "demain".

blocks.heading: Plus-que-parfait in a story
blocks.body: In narration, the plus-que-parfait explains the cause or background of a past event: what had happened earlier. It often follows verbs of discovery in the passé composé — you find out NOW what had happened BEFORE.

examples.french: J'ai compris pourquoi elle était partie.
examples.english: I understood why she had left.

examples.french: Il a avoué qu'il avait menti.
examples.english: He admitted that he had lied.

examples.french: Quand nous sommes rentrés, le voleur avait déjà disparu.
examples.english: When we got home, the thief had already disappeared.

examples.french: Elle portait la robe qu'elle avait achetée à Nice.
examples.english: She was wearing the dress she had bought in Nice.

blocks.tip: Négation wraps the auxiliary: "il n'avait pas prévenu", "elle n'était pas venue".

passages.title: Le mystère de la valise
passages.french:
Lundi matin, Claire est arrivée à l'aéroport de Lyon, fatiguée mais contente.
Elle avait passé une semaine magnifique au Portugal.
La veille, elle avait fait sa valise avec soin : cadeaux, photos, souvenirs.
Mais devant le tapis roulant, elle a attendu, attendu... rien.
Sa valise avait disparu.
Au comptoir, un employé lui a posé mille questions.
Avait-elle bien enregistré son bagage ? Avait-elle gardé son ticket ?
Claire s'est aperçue qu'elle avait laissé le ticket dans l'avion.
Heureusement, l'employé a retrouvé la trace de la valise dans l'ordinateur.
Elle était partie... à Madrid, avec un autre avion !
« On vous la livrera demain », a promis l'employé, désolé.
Le lendemain, la valise est arrivée chez Claire, intacte.
À l'intérieur, tout était là — sauf le fromage qu'elle avait acheté à Porto.
Claire n'a jamais su ce qui lui était arrivé.
passages.english:
Monday morning, Claire arrived at Lyon airport, tired but happy.
She had spent a wonderful week in Portugal.
The day before, she had packed her suitcase carefully: gifts, photos, souvenirs.
But at the baggage carousel, she waited and waited... nothing.
Her suitcase had disappeared.
At the counter, an employee asked her a thousand questions.
Had she checked in her bag properly? Had she kept her ticket?
Claire realized she had left the ticket on the plane.
Fortunately, the employee found a trace of the suitcase in the computer.
It had gone... to Madrid, on another plane!
"We'll deliver it to you tomorrow," the employee promised, apologetic.
The next day, the suitcase arrived at Claire's, intact.
Inside, everything was there — except the cheese she had bought in Porto.
Claire never found out what had happened to it.

lessons.title: Rebondissements
lessons.description: Structure a gripping story with connectors: alors que, pendant que, soudain and more.

blocks.heading: Simultaneity: pendant que, alors que, tandis que
blocks.body: "Pendant que" simply means two actions happen at the same time. "Alors que" and "tandis que" also mean "while", but often add contrast or surprise — something happens against the backdrop of something else. All three are followed by the indicative.

examples.french: Pendant que je cuisinais, il mettait la table.
examples.english: While I was cooking, he was setting the table.

examples.french: Alors que tout le monde dormait, elle est sortie sans bruit.
examples.english: While everyone was sleeping, she went out silently.

examples.french: Il est riche, tandis que son frère n'a rien.
examples.english: He is rich, whereas his brother has nothing.

examples.french: Alors que nous partions, le facteur est arrivé.
examples.english: Just as we were leaving, the postman arrived.

examples.french: Pendant que tu y es, achète du pain.
examples.english: While you're at it, buy some bread.

blocks.heading: Turning points: soudain, tout à coup, au moment où
blocks.body: To launch a plot twist — un rebondissement — French uses "soudain" or "tout à coup" followed by a passé composé. "Au moment où" pinpoints the exact moment, and "dès que" (as soon as) chains two events tightly.

examples.french: Soudain, une ombre est apparue derrière lui.
examples.english: Suddenly, a shadow appeared behind him.

examples.french: Tout à coup, toutes les lumières se sont éteintes.
examples.english: All of a sudden, all the lights went out.

examples.french: Au moment où il ouvrait la porte, le téléphone a sonné.
examples.english: Just as he was opening the door, the phone rang.

examples.french: Dès que le soleil s'est levé, nous avons repris la route.
examples.english: As soon as the sun rose, we set off again.

blocks.tip: "Soudain" and "tout à coup" are interchangeable. "Soudainement" exists but sounds heavier — storytellers prefer the short forms.

blocks.heading: Ordering a story: d'abord, puis, enfin
blocks.body: Give your story a skeleton with sequence words: "d'abord" (first), "puis" / "ensuite" (then), "enfin" or "finalement" (finally). "Au début" and "à la fin" frame the whole tale, and "la suite" is what comes next.

examples.french: D'abord, ils ont entendu un bruit dans la cave.
examples.english: First, they heard a noise in the cellar.

examples.french: Puis ils ont pris une lampe et sont descendus.
examples.english: Then they took a lamp and went down.

examples.french: Enfin, ils ont découvert la vérité.
examples.english: Finally, they discovered the truth.

examples.french: Au début, personne ne le croyait.
examples.english: At first, nobody believed him.

examples.french: Je vous raconterai la suite demain.
examples.english: I'll tell you the rest tomorrow.

blocks.heading: Which tense after each connector?
blocks.body: "Pendant que", "alors que" and "au moment où" usually introduce a background action in the imparfait, while the main clause carries the passé composé event. "Dès que" and "lorsque" typically link two passé composé events in sequence.

examples.french: Alors que je me douchais, on a coupé l'eau.
examples.english: While I was showering, the water was cut off.

examples.french: Dès que j'ai reçu ton message, je t'ai rappelé.
examples.english: As soon as I got your message, I called you back.

examples.french: Pendant que les invités dansaient, le gâteau brûlait dans le four.
examples.english: While the guests were dancing, the cake was burning in the oven.

examples.french: Lorsque le train s'est arrêté, tout le monde est descendu.
examples.english: When the train stopped, everyone got off.

blocks.tip: "Soudain" and "tout à coup" are adverbs, not conjunctions — they start a sentence and are followed directly by the event.

items.prompt: Launch a plot twist.
items.french: Soudain, quelqu'un a éteint toutes les lumières.
items.english: Suddenly, someone turned off all the lights.
items.tip: Pause dramatically after "Soudain" — French storytellers let the word hang in the air.

items.prompt: Describe two simultaneous actions.
items.french: Pendant que je travaillais, mon chat dormait sur le clavier.
items.english: While I was working, my cat was sleeping on the keyboard.
items.tip: "Pendant que" flows as one unit: pahn-dahn-kuh, with the stress on the verb that follows.

items.prompt: Wrap up a story.
items.french: Finalement, tout s'est bien terminé pour tout le monde.
items.english: In the end, everything turned out well for everyone.
items.tip: "Finalement" has four even syllables: fee-nahl-MAHN, with a light nasal ending.

passages.title: Une nuit dans la forêt
passages.french:
Ce week-end-là, Hugo et sa sœur Lise campaient dans la forêt de Fontainebleau.
D'abord, tout s'est passé comme prévu.
Ils ont monté la tente, allumé un petit feu et grillé des saucisses.
Pendant que Hugo rangeait les affaires, Lise observait les étoiles.
La nuit était douce et le silence, presque parfait.
Soudain, un craquement a retenti derrière les arbres.
Les deux jeunes se sont regardés sans bouger.
Alors que Hugo cherchait sa lampe, le bruit s'est rapproché.
Une ombre énorme est apparue entre les buissons...
Lise a poussé un cri — puis elle a éclaté de rire.
C'était un sanglier, aussi surpris qu'eux, qui s'est enfui aussitôt.
Dès que leur cœur s'est calmé, ils sont retournés près du feu.
Finalement, ils ont passé la meilleure nuit de leur vie.
Le lendemain, ils racontaient déjà leur aventure à tout le monde.
passages.english:
That weekend, Hugo and his sister Lise were camping in the Fontainebleau forest.
At first, everything went as planned.
They put up the tent, lit a small fire and grilled sausages.
While Hugo was putting things away, Lise was watching the stars.
The night was mild and the silence almost perfect.
Suddenly, a crack rang out behind the trees.
The two young people looked at each other without moving.
While Hugo was looking for his flashlight, the noise came closer.
A huge shadow appeared between the bushes...
Lise let out a scream — then she burst out laughing.
It was a wild boar, as surprised as they were, which fled at once.
As soon as their hearts calmed down, they went back to the fire.
In the end, they had the best night of their lives.
The next day, they were already telling everyone about their adventure.
